title: Extend the snapshot data model with derived/provenance fields
description: Add optional per-Kpi fields previousValue?: MetricValue, delta?: string, sourceDeltas?: SubReading[], carried?: boolean, and Snapshot.lastEditedAt?: string (ISO) to shared/types.ts. All optional for backward compatibility with existing locked snapshots — older snapshots that lack them must still load and render. No behaviour is wired here; the fields are the contract the pull/seed, delta, autosave, and carried-pill tickets all write to and read from (ADR-004/ADR-005).
acceptanceCriteria: The Kpi interface exposes optional previousValue, delta, sourceDeltas and carried fields, and Snapshot exposes an optional lastEditedAt
A snapshot JSON object omitting every new field still satisfies the Snapshot type (all new fields optional)
sourceDeltas reuses the existing SubReading {label,value} shape rather than a new type
rationale: Every derived/provenance behaviour (delta, previous value, per-source deltas, carried, last-edited) must be persisted onto the self-contained snapshot rather than recomputed at render (ADR-004/005). Landing the optional fields first gives the pull, builder and read-only tickets a stable contract to write and read, and keeps the type change isolated from the behaviours that populate it.

title: Add MBR sub-route steps and dispatch each to its screen slot
description: Extend parseHash so a #mbr hash reads rest[0] into a new Route.step field ('start' | 'collect' | 'build' | 'preview'), defaulting to 'start' when absent, mirroring the existing #locked/<id> [head,...rest] parse. Keep the single 'mbr' RouteView (App's DEV gate and KNOWN_VIEWS unchanged). MbrBuilderView switches on route.step and renders a distinct slot per step (thin placeholders here; the Reviews/Collect/Build/Preview tickets fill each slot). This is the routing substrate the four MBR screens mount into.
acceptanceCriteria: parseHash('#mbr') returns { view: 'mbr', step: 'start' } and parseHash('#mbr/collect'|'#mbr/build'|'#mbr/preview') return the matching step
An unknown #mbr/<x> segment falls back to the 'start' step
MbrBuilderView renders a different step slot for each of start/collect/build/preview based on route.step
App still resolves view==='mbr' to the Default view on a production (non-DEV) build (gate unchanged)
rationale: The four screens are namespaced sub-routes under one DEV-gated 'mbr' view so App's production dead-code guard and useHashRoute's KNOWN_VIEWS stay untouched. Building the step parse + switch skeleton first gives every screen ticket a slot to plug into without each re-editing the router, and lets them land as siblings rather than a queue.

title: Add pure metric-value parsing and delta computation helpers
description: Add a pure, unit-tested helper parseMetricValue(raw): { n, unit } | null that strips leading inequality/qualifier tokens (<= >= < > ~ approx), matches the first signed decimal (-?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?, commas stripped) and normalizes the trailing unit (% days s /day h m etc.), plus a computeDelta helper that returns a display string ONLY when both current and previous parse to a number AND share the same normalized unit, and null otherwise. For cohort SubReading[], provide per-label diffing (match by label, order only as tie-break). No IO, no Date, no import.meta.env — importable by both the browser and any Node caller.
acceptanceCriteria: parseMetricValue('<= 1 day') and parseMetricValue('~9.4h') return the numeric value with the normalized unit; parseMetricValue('WIP') returns null
computeDelta returns null (neutral, no arrow) when either side is unparseable or the normalized units differ
computeDelta of two same-unit numbers returns a signed magnitude string with the shared unit
cohort diffing matches sub-readings by label, not by array position
rationale: The free-text MetricValue corpus (scalars, %, durations, rates, inequalities, WIP) can only be diffed safely by parse-then-compare with unit guarding, returning a neutral placeholder for incomparable values. Isolating the pure helper lets the pull-seed, per-KPI re-collect, manual-edit and cohort tickets all compute deltas the same way and be tested without a DOM.

title: Change the off-track status marker to an X shape app-wide
description: Per ADR-006, change STATUS_META.negative.shape from 'diamond' to a new 'x' silhouette in src/lib/status.ts (the single source of truth for status shape), add a matching .status-dot--x rule to src/styles.css that draws an X distinct from the on-track filled circle without relying on colour, and update the disk-reading shape tests (status.shape.test.ts and styles.status-dot.test.ts) that currently assert/iterate 'diamond'. The other four markers (circle/triangle/ring/half-circle) are unchanged. This intentionally updates the off-track marker everywhere the app renders status.

acceptanceCriteria.text: STATUS_META.negative.shape is 'x' and the StatusMeta shape union includes 'x'
src/styles.css defines a .status-dot--x rule that renders an X silhouette (two crossed strokes), visibly unlike the filled on-track circle by shape alone
acceptanceCriteria.drawnAt: #screen-builder, the off-track status marker on the Ship Confidence 'Flaky test rate' row

acceptanceCriteria.text: The four other status shapes remain circle/triangle/ring/half-circle
The disk-reading shape tests assert 'x' for negative instead of 'diamond' and the suite stays green

rationale: The acceptance criteria mandate an X for colour-independent distinctness from the on-track circle. Because STATUS_META is the one source of truth for shape, editing it there is the minimal correct change and necessarily updates the marker app-wide; the two disk-reading tests pin the old 'diamond' and must move in the same slice. It is independent of the MBR screens, so it lands in parallel.

When an unlocked draft for the next month already exists on disk, the card offers 'Continue draft' (resume in place) instead of a reseeding 'Pull data & start'. Pull data & start navigates to #mbr/collect; View opens #locked/<id>; new drafts mint their id via nextDraftId(existingIds, today) (date-keyed YYYY-MM-DD.N, never a bare YYYY-MM).

title: Build the collection screen and seed the pulled draft
description: Implement the #mbr/collect (step 'collect') screen and the draft it produces. Drive 'Pull data & start' off the REAL per-KPI endpoint POST /__collect/<kpiId> (collectKpi, concurrency 1), aggregated per bucket as 'Queued → Collecting… → N values pulled' with the progress bar advancing as each KPI finishes, a Cancel control returning to #mbr, and a 'Continue to builder' button disabled until the pull finishes (then navigating to #mbr/build). Auto vs manual is derived from a trim-strict non-empty aiUpdateInstructions resolved from the roster (the resolveAutomatable predicate), NOT WIRED_METRIC_IDS. The pull seeds a draft snapshot in which each KPI carries: a fresh value (or the previous published MBR's value/status when the pull returns no fresh reading — carried=true), target frozen from config, previousValue from the last published MBR, a computed delta (via t-003), per-source sourceDeltas for cohorts, status seeded from the scorecard, and asOf = pull date. A KPI absent from the current pull collapses (failure or empty) to carried; an emitted value (even unchanged) is fresh.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each bucket row cycles through a Queued chip, a Collecting… chip with a spinner, and an 'N values pulled' chip as its KPIs finish, with the progress bar advancing per bucket
acceptanceCriteria.drawnAt: #screen-collect, the collect-list rows and the progress bar above them

acceptanceCriteria.text: 'Continue to builder' is disabled until every bucket has finished, then navigates to #mbr/build; Cancel returns to #mbr
acceptanceCriteria.drawnAt: #continueBtn and the Cancel control in the collect-list footer

acceptanceCriteria.text: The seeded draft freezes target from config, records previousValue from the last published MBR, and stamps a computed delta per KPI
A KPI whose pull returns no fresh reading (failure or empty) carries the previous MBR's value/status forward with carried=true; an emitted value clears carried
The automatable partition driving which KPIs are collected is derived from trim-strict non-empty aiUpdateInstructions resolved from the roster, not from WIRED_METRIC_IDS

rationale: 'Pull data & start' is one cohesive behaviour: run the real per-KPI collection and produce the seeded draft the builder then edits. The seeding (target-freeze, previousValue, delta, carried, status, asOf) is inseparable from the pull that yields it, so it lives here rather than as a horizontal helper layer. It reads the new model fields (t-001), the delta helper (t-003) and mounts on the step router (t-002).

title: Build the redesigned builder shell and insight authoring loop
description: Implement the #mbr/build (step 'build') screen matching the mockup: eyebrow 'Monthly Business Review'; title 'MBR builder · {month}'; the subtitle 'Assemble this month's review from the live scorecard. Add an insight to each KPI, then lock the month to publish it.'; a toolbar with a Preview button and an amber 'Lock month' primary button (NO theme toggle — the builder follows the app's global theme per CONTEXT.md; toolbar click handlers for Preview/Lock are wired by later tickets). An amber draft banner with a warning dot reading 'Draft — changes are saved locally as you go' and a 'Last edited {t} · N of M buckets complete' meta (absolute UTC-pinned formatDate timestamp). An 'Insights added — N of M KPIs' completion bar under the banner where a KPI counts as done when its insight text is non-empty. Bucket cards with a 4px accent, header 'N KPIs' and an 'N of M insights' sub-count (no per-bucket lock badge or unlock control). Each KPI row: name (with a purple 'Carried' clock pill when kpi.carried), a value-display cell (scalar or cohort with the stored delta), an editable status select over the five silhouettes (On track/Watch/Off track/Tracking/WIP), and an insight textarea that autosaves on blur and debounced at 800ms while typing (flush on blur/before-unload) via PUT /__data/snapshots/<id>, stamping Snapshot.lastEditedAt; a non-empty insight gets the distinct filled background. Remove the old New MBR / Refresh all data / handle+amendment lock UI. Update the existing MbrBuilderView tests to the new flow.

It replaces the old builder wholesale; keeping the toolbar buttons here (wired later) lets those behaviours land as dependents rather than rewriting the layout.

title: Add per-KPI collect controls to wired builder value cells
description: In the builder's value cell for automatable (wired) KPIs, render the value, target, a 'vs last MBR' scalar delta, an 'Auto' tag, and Collect / Re-collect / Try again controls that drive POST /__collect/<kpiId> (collectKpi) with Collecting… (spinner), '✓ Updated', and 'Collection failed' state chips, plus a 'was {old} · as of {date}' line after a successful (re-)collect. A successful re-collect applies the fresh value, stamps asOf, moves the prior value into previousValue and recomputes that KPI's delta via t-003. Reuses the Update-KPIs collection vocabulary rather than inventing a second pipeline.

acceptanceCriteria.drawnAt: #screen-builder, the Deployment frequency row's value cell in the Velocity bucket

rationale: Per-KPI automated collection is a distinct behaviour from the shell's static value display: it owns the Collect/Re-collect/Try-again lifecycle, the state chips and the delta recompute-on-collect. It extends the value cell the shell (t-007) established, uses the delta helper (t-003) and the persisted previousValue/delta fields (t-001), and reuses the shipping Update-KPIs collect vocabulary rather than a second pipeline.

title: Make unwired builder KPI values inline-editable
description: In the builder, render manual (unwired) KPI values as an inline editable input with its unit, the target, a 'vs last MBR' delta, a 'From default view · edit to override' note, a 'Manual' tag, and an amber 'needs value' state when empty — with no per-value lock/asOf commit step. The value is seeded from the KPI's committed value carried forward (manualSeedValue, matched by stable id) and stays editable until lock; 'As of' defaults to the pull date. Editing the value recomputes its delta automatically via t-003 (deltas are never hand-typed) and clears carried on that KPI (a hand-entered value is fresh, not carried).

acceptanceCriteria.text: A manual KPI value renders as an editable input with its unit, a 'target N' line and a 'vs last MBR' delta
acceptanceCriteria.drawnAt: #screen-builder, the PR review latency row's value cell in the Velocity bucket

acceptanceCriteria.text: Editing a manual value recomputes its delta automatically and never lets the delta be hand-typed
Editing a manual value clears carried on that KPI, and there is no per-value 'Lock in value' + As-of commit step
'As of' defaults to the pull date when a manual value is entered

rationale: Inline manual editing is a distinct behaviour from automated collection: no source, no lock/asOf step, delta recomputed and carried cleared on edit. It extends the shell's value cell (t-007), uses the delta helper (t-003) and the persisted delta/carried fields (t-001). Keeping it separate from the wired-collect ticket keeps each value-cell variant cohesive and independently testable.

title: Show per-source deltas on multi-value builder KPIs
description: In the builder, render a multi-value (cohort) KPI's value cell as the full label/value cohort breakdown (no collapsing, expander or averaged headline), with each source row carrying its own 'change vs last MBR' delta (up / down / no-change) matched to the previous published MBR by label, and a 'change vs last MBR' caption under the list. Per-source deltas read from the persisted sourceDeltas and recompute (via t-003, matched by label) when a cohort sub-row is edited. When a source has no comparable prior reading, its row renders a neutral placeholder rather than a fabricated 'no change'.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cohort KPI lists every source as a label/value row with its own delta and a 'change vs last MBR' caption below the list
acceptanceCriteria.drawnAt: #screen-builder, the LTC P75 cohort value cell in the Velocity bucket

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each source's delta is matched to the previous published MBR by label, not by array position
A source with no comparable prior reading renders a neutral placeholder rather than 'no change'

rationale: A cohort KPI's per-source trend is its own behaviour: it diffs each SubReading against the prior MBR by label (positional subtraction is undefined because SubReading has no id) and renders a per-row delta column the scalar cell does not have. It extends the shell's value cell (t-007), reads sourceDeltas (t-001) and uses the label-matched delta helper (t-003).

title: Add the auto-only Refresh-all warning box and progress strip
description: Add the builder's 'Update all automatically' control laid out as the mockup draws it: an amber .warn-line box carrying ONLY the caveat text — it collects KPIs with automated instructions ('11 of 14' via automatableCount over draft.buckets.flatMap(b=>b.kpis)), leaves the manual KPIs unchanged, and seeds manual values from the default view — with the 'Update all automatically' button inside the box, and a SEPARATE indeterminate .update-progress strip sibling below the action bar (not nested in the box). The sweep re-runs the per-KPI collect pipeline (from t-008) for automatable KPIs only in order, recomputing their deltas; every manual value and every insight is preserved untouched, and a KPI that returns no fresh value stays as it was (Carried preserved).

The sweep refreshes automatable KPIs only, recomputing their deltas, while every manual value and every insight is preserved and a still-empty KPI stays Carried

rationale: The auto-only re-pull is a distinct bulk behaviour with its own warning-box + indeterminate-strip layout and its own preservation guarantees (manual values and insights untouched, Carried preserved). It reuses the per-KPI collect pipeline established in t-008 rather than building a second one, and the delta helper (t-003) to recompute swept KPIs.

title: Add the month-only lock, read-only state and builder dialogs
description: Implement the per-month lock model and the three centered overlay dialogs. The amber 'Lock month' toolbar button opens a 'Lock {Month Year}?' dialog whose summary reflects insight completeness; the month cannot lock while any KPI has a blank insight (the completion meter is exactly the lock gate), and locking sets status:'locked', lockedBy = null and lockedAt, persisting the same file. When the month is locked, ALL buckets render read-only solely because the month is locked: static values, status shown as a label (not a select), insight shown as text (not a textarea); the only way back to editable is unlocking the whole month. The draft banner's 'Discard draft' button opens a 'Discard this draft?' danger dialog ('Keep editing' / 'Discard draft') that on confirm clears the draft and returns to #mbr. An unlock-month dialog is a simple confirm with no note field. There is no per-bucket lock/unlock and no 'Unlock this bucket?' dialog. All dialogs are centered over a dimmed backdrop, each with a coloured icon badge, dismissable by backdrop click or Esc.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The lock action is blocked while any KPI has a blank insight, so a published month never contains an insight-less KPI
Locking sets lockedBy to null (no handle field) and renders every bucket read-only — static values, status as a label, insight as text — until the month is unlocked
acceptanceCriteria.drawnAt: #screen-builder, the locked (read-only) Ship Confidence and Platform Health bucket rows

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every dialog is dismissable by backdrop click or Esc

rationale: Month-only locking, the read-only-when-locked rendering and the three dialogs are one cohesive commitment behaviour: the completion meter, the lock gate and what publishes all express the same condition (ADR-003). It deliberately drops the mockup's per-bucket lock affordances and the lockedBy handle. It wires the Lock and Discard controls the shell (t-007) placed, so it depends on the shell.

title: Share one read-only render for Preview and published View
description: Give Preview and View one shared read-only presentation component, differing only in source (live draft vs immutable snapshot), reusing the existing LockedView render path (ADR-002). The builder toolbar's Preview button navigates to #mbr/preview and renders the current draft read-only exactly as it will publish, with a way to back out to #mbr/build without locking; the Reviews 'View' button continues to open a published month at #locked/<id> in that same rendering. In LockedView, hide the 'Locked by {handle}' provenance line when lockedBy is null (never print 'Locked by —') while RETAINING the Amendments section unchanged so historical snapshots that carry a handle/amendments still render faithfully.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The builder's Preview button navigates to #mbr/preview and renders the current draft read-only in the same presentation the locked buckets use, with a back-out that returns to #mbr/build without locking
acceptanceCriteria.drawnAt: #screen-builder, the Preview toolbar button and the locked (read-only) bucket rendering it mirrors

acceptanceCriteria.text: Preview and View render through one shared read-only component, differing only in draft-vs-snapshot source
LockedView hides the 'Locked by' provenance line when lockedBy is null and never prints 'Locked by —'
The Amendments section still renders for a historical snapshot that carries amendments

rationale: Preview and View must render identically to what publishes, so they share one read-only component reusing the LockedView path (ADR-002), guaranteeing Preview is faithful to the published output. Hiding the null lockedBy line (the handle field the redesign removes) while keeping Amendments preserves faithful rendering of already-committed historical snapshots. It wires the shell's Preview button and mounts on the step router.
